correctness.rationale: For a=b/v, d=1+zeta-ell>0, R=r(ell), the exact stationary generator gives m1=a/(d+R) and m2=2(ell+a)a/((d+R)(2d+R)). The uniform v->infinity limit at fixed zeta gives the stated integrated formula, and v Var(N)->b/(d+R)+2ell b/((d+R)(2d+R)). Self-consistency yields integrated density rho. Strict beta denominator and nu<1 give rho->finite. At high fitness x=1-ell, the singular integrand is asymptotic to 2/((zeta+Cx^nu)(2zeta+Cx^nu)). Dominated convergence for nu<1/2, two-sided log comparison at nu=1/2, and scaling x=(zeta/C)^(1/nu)y with integrable y^(-2nu) tail for nu>1/2 prove all three regimes and amplitudes. The full CHECK.py package uses exact rational identities, independently integrated finite-chain dynamics and asymptotic quadrature as consistency checks, not replacements for proof.

value.rationale: The within-site ordered pair count is a natural local crowding/susceptibility observable for particle populations and link accumulation. Its universal nu=1/2 critical point occurs strictly below the motivating paper’s nu=1 density-condensation boundary: bounded mean population coexists with divergent local pair intensity. The sharp logarithmic and power-law constants survive a broad class of fitness densities and reset profiles. This is a qualitatively distinct phase boundary, not an arbitrary parameter increment or an unmotivated invariant. No full-network or physical efficiency implication is asserted.
